title: First, moreover, on the contrary
goal: Order, add, contrast and prove points in an argument, and close it with the right concluding phrase.

intro.text: Signposts make an argument easy to follow. *Öncelikle* opens it, *üstelik* and *kaldı ki* add weight, *aksine* turns a negative into its opposite, *nitekim* brings evidence and *zira* gives a reason in formal writing. *Sonuç olarak*, *özetle* and *kısacası* close it.

vocab.en: first of all; as a priority
on the one hand … on the other hand
besides, and anyway (adds an argument that settles the matter)
on the contrary; unlike, contrary to (after the genitive: beklentilerin aksine)
quite the opposite, on the contrary
indeed, as a matter of fact (bringing confirming evidence)
to sum up, to wrap up (toparlarsak: to sum up); to tidy up

exercises.text: Fiyatlar düşmedi; ___ son bir yılda iki katına çıktı.
exercises.en: Prices didn't fall; on the contrary, they doubled in the last year.
exercises.explain: *Aksine* follows a negative and puts the opposite in its place. *Üstelik* would add a point in the same direction; *zira* would give a reason.

exercises.en: Contrary to expectations, the novel sold very well.

accept: in

reject.why: *Aksine* takes the genitive, like a possessed noun: *beklentilerin aksine*.
*Aksine* takes the genitive: *beklentilerin aksine*. The ablative goes with *farklı*: *beklentilerden farklı*.

exercises.hint: **Contrary to X**: X takes the same case as an owner.
exercises.explain: *X-in aksine* means **contrary to X** or **unlike X**: *beklentilerin aksine*, *ağabeyinin aksine*.

exercises.prompt: On the one hand I want to live in the city, on the other hand I miss my village.
accept: Bir yandan şehirde yaşamak istiyorum, öte yandan köyümü özlüyorum.
bir yandan şehirde yaşamak istiyorum, öte yandan köyümü özledim.
bir yandan şehirde yaşamak istiyorum, öte yandan da köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
bir yandan şehirde yaşamak istiyorum, diğer yandan (da) köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
bir yandan kentte yaşamak istiyorum, [öte|diğer] yandan (da) köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
Ben bir yandan [şehirde|kentte] yaşamak istiyorum, [öte|diğer] yandan (da) köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
(Ben) bir taraftan [şehirde|kentte] yaşamak istiyorum, [öte|diğer] taraftan (da) köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
(Ben) bir yandan [şehirde|kentte] yaşamak istiyorum, bir yandan da köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
Bir yandan ben [şehirde|kentte] yaşamak istiyorum, [öte|diğer] yandan (da) köyümü [özlüyorum|özledim].
exercises.explain: *Bir yandan … öte yandan* sets two sides of one situation against each other; *diğer yandan* and *bir taraftan … diğer taraftan* are just as common.

exercises.prompt: Herkes bu kitabın çok satacağını söylüyordu; nitekim öyle de oldu.
accept: Everyone said this book would sell a lot; and indeed, it did.
Everyone said this book would sell a lot [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
Everyone said this book would sell a lot and in fact it did.
Everyone said this book would sell a lot and sure enough it did.
Everyone said this book would sell a lot and as it turned out it did.
Everyone said this book would sell well (and) [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
Everyone said this book would sell very well (and) [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
Everyone said that this book would sell [a lot|well|very well] (and) [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
Everyone was saying (that) this book would sell [a lot|well|very well] (and) [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
Everybody [said|was saying] (that) this book would sell [a lot|well|very well] (and) [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
[Everyone|Everybody] had been saying (that) this book would sell [a lot|well|very well] (and) [indeed|in fact|sure enough|as it turned out] it did.
[Everyone|Everybody] [said|was saying] (that) this book would sell [a lot|well|very well], and [it did|so it did|that is what happened|that is exactly what happened].
exercises.explain: *Nitekim* brings a fact that confirms what was said before: here, the prediction came true. *Öyle de oldu* is **and so it did**.

exercises.question: You are writing an essay. Which sentence gives a reason in a formal style?
options: Bu öneri kabul edilmemelidir, zira maliyeti çok yüksektir.
Bu öneri kabul edilmemeli, çünkü çok pahalı ya.
Bu öneriyi kabul etmeyelim bence, çok pahalı.
Bu öneri kabul edilmemelidir, nitekim maliyeti çok yüksektir.

why.1: Correct, but *ya* and the plain *çok pahalı* belong to conversation.
why.2: Everyday speech: *bence*, the optative *etmeyelim* and no `-DIr`.
why.3: *Nitekim* brings evidence that confirms a claim, not the reason for it. For **because**, write *zira*.

exercises.explain: *Zira* (because) is formal and comes after the claim; with `-mAlIdIr` and `-DIr` the sentence suits an essay.

exercises.prompt: In short, we are not coming tonight.
accept: Kısacası, bu akşam gelmiyoruz.
Kısacası bu akşam gelmeyeceğiz.
Kısacası bu gece [gelmiyoruz|gelmeyeceğiz].
Kısacası biz [bu akşam|bu gece] [gelmiyoruz|gelmeyeceğiz].
Özetle (biz) [bu akşam|bu gece] [gelmiyoruz|gelmeyeceğiz].
Sözün kısası (biz) [bu akşam|bu gece] [gelmiyoruz|gelmeyeceğiz].
[Kısacası|Özetle|Sözün kısası] [bu akşam|bu gece] biz [gelmiyoruz|gelmeyeceğiz].
exercises.explain: *Kısacası* puts what came before into one line; between friends it can sound a little impatient. *Sözün kısası* (to cut a long story short) works too.

exercises.text: Hava çok soğuk; ___ yağmur da yağıyor. Bugün yürüyüşe çıkmayalım.
exercises.en: It's very cold; what's more, it's raining too. Let's not go for a walk today.
exercises.explain: *Üstelik* adds a further point in the same direction, often with *dA* on the new element: *yağmur da*. *Aksine* would need a negative before it; *nitekim* would bring evidence for a claim.

exercises.question: *Bu projeyi bir ayda bitiremeyiz; kaldı ki bütçemiz de yok.* What does *kaldı ki* add?
options: a further point that settles the matter
a contrast with the first point
the reason for the first point
a summary of what was said

why.1: There is no contrast: both points argue against the project.
why.2: For a reason, Turkish uses *çünkü* or *zira*; *kaldı ki* adds a new, independent argument.
why.3: A summary would start with *kısacası* or *özetle*.

exercises.explain: *Kaldı ki* (besides, and anyway) adds an argument strong enough on its own: even if the project could be finished in a month, there is no money for it.

exercises.prompt: Film sıkıcı değildi; aksine, çok eğlenceliydi.
accept: The film was not boring; on the contrary, it was a lot of fun.
The film was not boring; on the contrary it was great fun.
The film was not boring; on the contrary it was very entertaining.
The film was not boring; on the contrary it was really entertaining.
The film was not boring; on the contrary it was very enjoyable.
The film was not boring; on the contrary it was really enjoyable.
The film was not boring; on the contrary it was really fun.
The film was not boring; quite the opposite it was [a lot of fun|great fun|very entertaining|really entertaining|very enjoyable|really enjoyable|really fun].
The film was not boring; quite the contrary it was [a lot of fun|great fun|very entertaining|really entertaining|very enjoyable|really enjoyable|really fun].
The film was not boring; in fact it was [a lot of fun|great fun|very entertaining|really entertaining|very enjoyable|really enjoyable|really fun].

The movie was not boring; [on the contrary|quite the opposite|quite the contrary|in fact] it was [a lot of fun|great fun|very entertaining|really entertaining|very enjoyable|really enjoyable|really fun].
It was not a boring [film|movie]; [on the contrary|quite the opposite|in fact] it was [a lot of fun|great fun|very entertaining|very enjoyable|really enjoyable].
exercises.explain: *Aksine* follows the negative *sıkıcı değildi* and puts its opposite in its place.

exercises.prompt: Unlike her brother, Elif is very calm.
accept: Ağabeyinin aksine Elif çok sakin.
Ağabeyinin aksine Elif çok sakindir.
Ağabeyinin tersine Elif çok sakin(dir).
Abisinin [aksine|tersine] Elif çok sakin(dir).
Kardeşinin [aksine|tersine] Elif çok sakin(dir).
Erkek kardeşinin [aksine|tersine] Elif çok sakin(dir).
Elif [ağabeyinin|abisinin|kardeşinin|erkek kardeşinin] [aksine|tersine] çok sakin(dir).
Elif çok sakin, [ağabeyinin|abisinin|kardeşinin|erkek kardeşinin] [aksine|tersine].
exercises.explain: *Aksine* after a genitive means **unlike** or **contrary to**: *ağabeyinin aksine*. *Tersine* works the same way.

exercises.task: Write a short paragraph (four or five sentences) for or against this claim: *Kitap okumak için en iyi yer telefondur.* Open with *öncelikle*, add a point with *üstelik* or *kaldı ki*, answer the other side with *aksine* or *öte yandan*, and close with *sonuç olarak* or *kısacası*.
models: Öncelikle, telefon her zaman yanımızda: otobüste, kuyrukta, her yerde okuyabiliriz. Üstelik e-kitaplar çoğu zaman basılı kitaplardan daha ucuz. Telefonda okumanın gözleri yorduğu söyleniyor; öte yandan ekranın ışığını ayarlayarak bu sorunu azaltmak mümkün. Kaldı ki hiç okumamaktansa telefonda okumak daha iyidir. Sonuç olarak, telefon kitap okumak için en pratik yer.

Öncelikle, telefon dikkatimizi sürekli dağıtıyor: her bildirimde kitabı bırakıp mesajlara bakıyoruz. Üstelik küçük bir ekranda uzun bir roman okumak gözleri yoruyor. Telefon okumayı kolaylaştırmıyor; aksine, zorlaştırıyor. Kısacası, iyi bir kitap için en iyi yer yine kâğıt sayfalar.
checklist: *Üstelik* or *kaldı ki* adds a point in the same direction
*Aksine* follows a negative; *öte yandan* brings in the other side
The last sentence starts with *sonuç olarak* or *kısacası* and states your position
Neutral or formal Turkish throughout: no *ya*, no fillers
